messages:
li (evals): Nightly eval alert: assistant-formatting promptset fail rate jumped from ~0.6% to 18% after the weight rollforward this morning. Failures are JSON parse errors when tooling tries to parse the function_call payload. Sample below.

marta (ml-eng): :eyes: paste one of the bad outputs plz

li (evals): ```
{"choice": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "{\"name\": \"create_ticket\", \"arguments\": {\"title\": \"Payment issue\", \"metadata\": \"\\u200bpriority:high\"}}"}}
```

li (evals): Note the invisible U+200B in metadata value and also an extra escaping layer — our parser expects JSON directly in content or function_call.arguments, not a doubly encoded string. Reproducer: curl against nightly-canary with the same prompt, see same pattern.

ken (serving): Did the tokenizer change in the rollforward? We didn't change quantization. Any tokenizer commits in the bundle?

marta (ml-eng): No tokenizer commits in the deploy, it was weights-only. But weight delta included a tiny vocab reorder from the upstream vendor (they said minor). Could be causing subtle serialization differences?

sofia (prod-ml): Canary-bot posted an alert earlier:
canary-bot: [alert] assistant-formatting promptset A/B diff: 0.6% -> 17.9% JSON_parse_error.

li (evals): Full repro command I used locally:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY' -d '{"model":"mymodel-rollfwd","input":"${PROMPT}"}'
```
Then run our parse script: `python tools/parse_function_calls.py out.json` -> parser raises JSONDecodeError at char index where U+200B is embedded.

ken (serving): That smells like the model is emitting zero-width separators inside strings for some reason (maybe training artifact). Can we confirm outputs differ between pre-rollforward and post-rollforward for the exact same seed/prompt?

li (evals): Yes. Diffed outputs for 200 samples: 0 -> had plain JSON; post -> 18% have either extra escaping or invisible chars. Example diff (pre | post):
```
pre: {"arguments": {"desc": "User can't login"}}
post: {"arguments": "{\\\"desc\\\": \"User can't login\"}"}
```

marta (ml-eng): Looks like doubling of encoding layer: sometimes the model returns a string containing JSON rather than an object token stream. Could be prompt interpretation change from weight update. Maybe the model learned to be more conservative and serialize to string.

sofia (prod-ml): Impact: downstream function-call handler fails and we route to fallback which increases latency and error rate. Customer-facing incidents possible if the trend continues.

ken (serving): Quick triage plan: 1) run golden prompt set on pre-rollforward binary + current weights snapshot used last night (to confirm weights cause it), 2) run same on pre-rollforward weights on new binary to rule out serving runtime, 3) capture token-level logits around the JSON tokens to see whether quoting tokens changed. I'll spin up these jobs.

li (evals): I've queued the golden prompt job on our eval infra (job id: eval-349876-01). It will include token-level dumps.

marta (ml-eng): If it's just more frequent string-serialization, a short-term mitigation: add tolerant parsing in our function-call handler: attempt to json.loads twice (if first fails and value is a string, unescape and parse again), and add a small post-processing to strip common invisible chars (U+200B, U+FEFF). I'll draft a small patch. :hammer:

sofia (prod-ml): Patch sounds reasonable as a stopgap, but let's not mask root cause. Also add an eval alert that triggers when function_call parse errors spike.

li (evals): Results are in for the initial job (partial): token dumps show the model emits an extra `"` and backslashes sequence before the argument JSON for the failing cases. Log snippet: ```... 0x22 0x5c 0x22 ...``` which maps to `"` sequence — consistent with double-encoding.

ken (serving): Thanks. That points to behavior change in how the model chooses to represent structured outputs. Could be due to final-layer biases in the new weights. I'll open an internal rollback candidate if we confirm weights-only cause.

marta (ml-eng): Also checking prompt engineering: our assistant system prompt includes `Respond with JSON object for function calls` — maybe model became more literal and wraps in a string to avoid breaking system constraints. I'll test softened priming: allow either object or JSON string and see score differences.

canary-bot: [info] eval-349876-01 partial results: 18% double-encoded JSON, 1.2% invisible unicode characters detected.

li (evals): Immediate action items:
- ken: run weight-vs-binary split tests, confirm root cause (assigned)
- marta: open a quick tolerant-parse PR and add unicode strip for U+200B/U+FEFF (assigned)
- sofia: add alert for function_call parse error >1% (assigned)
- li: rerun full promptset with token dumps and attach diffs (assigned)

marta (ml-eng): I'll also add a small eval that runs on production traffic sampling to estimate customer impact.

sofia (prod-ml): If rollback confirmed, coordinate with infra for a staged rollback; if not, we'll aim for a controlled patch and long-term model retrain/curation note.

li (evals): Will post follow-ups when job completes. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
